post.description: Native callers require native.account.read and request proof, and can target only their current family/client/app/device. A normal browser can approve an explicit owned nativeSessionId; restricted-browser credentials are denied. The family must remain valid, the actor must still be staff with required bindings, and every requested action must pass the current policy/scope/permission intersection. Confirmation may instead come from a separate same-site/account browser session created within five minutes via passkey, +mfa or +2fa; native-origin sessions cannot supply that independent evidence. consent=true and 1..7 unique actions are mandatory. get.description: Action users.read; consented OAuth scope native.admin.users.read; current authority user:list. Requires nativeAccessToken AND X-Native-Admin-Grant, plus all three signed native proof headers. The nag_ grant is independent of the access token, expires within 300 seconds (or earlier native family expiry), and is not extended by refresh. Each request rechecks site/user/family/client/app/device binding, enabled App policy and its exact revision, selected action, current OAuth consent/scope, active device/application/backing session, current projected staff permissions and mandatory admin bindings. The equivalent browser action must be available on this site; a main-site role alone gives no subsite staff authority. Named services enforce target data scope. The projected actor stays private to this handler; ordinary native roles and /api/admin access remain restricted. Missing, expired, revoked, mismatched or obsolete-policy grants return envelope code 4284; policy/scope/permission failures return code 403. PageUsers returns data:{list,count} with the compact eight-field projection. Query filtering, shared-site membership projection and current target scope are the same as the named admin service. Requires Ed25519 signature over compact UTF-8 JSON without HTML escaping: ["sakura-native-request-v1", tenant issuer without trailing slash, clientId, deviceId (empty on new bind), exact HTTP method, exact request URI including query order, Content-Type, lowercase SHA256(token), lowercase SHA256(raw body), timestamp, nonce]. Body <=32 MiB. This is the native app protocol, not RFC DPoP. Query access_token is rejected. no-store. Cache-Control: no-store. Business and validation failures use HTTP 200 with nonzero envelope code; authentication/permission failures use envelope codes 401/403 unless an explicit HTTP response is listed.

post.description: Requires a real nativeAccessToken with explicit consented native.login.approve and signed request proof; normal and restricted-browser sessions are refused. The source native family, current user, client, app, device, OAuth consent and enabled browser policy are revalidated. Discovery binds the intent to the first exact user/client/app/device/family and policy revision; another device or family of the same user cannot take it over. Requires prior discovery and exact current deviceId. Signs compact UTF-8 DecisionMessage ["sakura-app-approval-v1", id, nonce, deviceId, "approve" or "deny", number, userVerified] in addition to the outer request proof. Approval requires consent=true, userVerified=true and the matching browser number; signed denial does not. Only pending, unexpired requests can transition once. post.description:
Authenticated administrator only. Strict single JSON object <=256 KiB; <=100 operations and <=8 KiB per body. The entire selection is prevalidated: only finite shared-table mutation routes of the same template/method, numeric IDs, and version queries for forced-action/points records. Arbitrary URLs, headers, recursive batches, mixed operations and duplicate route targets are rejected before mutation. Static user-status/invite routes validate and deduplicate target IDs, independent of JSON field order; each invite request selects exactly one ID. Processing is in-process without outbound HTTP, with a fresh Gin context and all original auth, tenant, permission, feature, data-scope, version, proof and audit checks for each record. Records commit independently; only outcomes are returned, never original data/secrets. A 30-second request budget stops unstarted items; completion refreshes the table once. No database migration.

Requires admin-panel authentication; additional handler restrictions are described above.

Fresh normal root identity, authenticated credential boundaries, exact owner/provider/connection tuple, current identity pool and transactional audit/outbox consistency remain mandatory. Challenge is site-bound, valid 5 minutes and has five reserved TOTP/recovery attempts. Requires still-enabled readable TOTP secret; each TOTP 30-second step is accepted once, recovery code consumed once. Successful proof atomically consumes challenge before session creation. rememberDevice requests optional trustedDevice grant; session remember comes from original first factor. No route-specific per-IP rate limiter is mounted here; challenge attempt budget applies. Business/validation/storage errors use HTTP 200 with nonzero code (normally 1); session and permission failures use code 401/403. A successful no-data mutation omits data. Explicit raw HTTP statuses below take precedence. R15: After all existing first/second-factor and setup checks, LoginResult may contain appApproval instead of a usable session. Maintain its initiating-browser continuation proof and sakura_app_login_browser context; separately admitted App response capability/number match completes it through the documented /api/app/v1/login-approvals operations. Missing/disabled/revoked responder or pending admission is not successful authentication.

post.description: Reuses the existing platform session via bearer or HttpOnly nowork_sso cookie, without creating another login or returning an API bearer. Cookie authentication is confined to this consent API and requires the resolved site's configured frontend Origin (or same-origin browser Fetch Metadata at that frontend host); cross-origin fetches include credentials. An explicit invalid bearer never falls back to the cookie. Responses are no-store. Code 401 means no active session, 4092 requests interactive reauthentication; neither is a platform logout. Source: middleware/oauth_consent.go, handler/oauth.go:Approve and service/account_gate_oauth.go. Session and exact request are revalidated. Success data contains responseMode and either redirect or formAction/formFields; the SPA performs navigation/form submission. Mandatory account completion is HTTP 200/code428 with typed data{actionRequired:true,route}; client preserves its safe authorization return route while completing the action. Omitted/false approve returns access_denied through the selected response mode with state. Reauthentication uses code 4092; issuer-resolution failure is direct OAuth HTTP 400 JSON.

post.description: No-store. Requires live site-bound OAuth state and its S256 browser proof; bind also requires the original authenticated browser. action=start initializes at most one in-memory flow per state; token verifies the user's own Skland account token through grant/cred/current-user. poll advances a QR no faster than every two seconds. Capacity 512, QR lifetime at most five minutes. Platform credentials/cookies are discarded and never returned. A verified response contains a short-lived internal single-use ticket, consumed by normal /api/oidc/callback with platform_verifier; registration, binding policy, App approval and MFA still apply. Multi-instance deployments require sticky routing for this short flow.

After verified settlement, callback POST JSON contains eventId='paid:'+orderNo, event='payment.paid', appId, orderNo, externalNo, amount (decimal string), currency, param. Signed X-Merchant-* headers use snapshotted key and same canonical rule. Receiver must answer 2xx with text success (<=1024 bytes); 8-second timeout, no redirects, max 12 attempts.

Signature is base64 RSA-SHA256 (PKCS#1 v1.5) over METHOD + newline + exact RequestURI + newline + timestamp + newline + nonce + newline + exact body + newline. Self-hosted relay compatibility, not official WeChat. Approved app, configured RSA verification key/serial/APIv3 key and IP allowlist required. Authorization<=4000 bytes; timestamp +/-300 seconds; nonce 8..64 bytes, replay-protected for 11 minutes; RequestURI<=4096 bytes; body<=16000 bytes; duplicate query fields rejected. Authenticated responses include Wechatpay-* signatures using relay certificate; authenticate failure is unsigned HTTP 401 SIGN_ERROR. Signing failure may produce empty HTTP 503. Use fresh nonce for retries. Certificate is self-signed relay trust anchor, encrypted using APIv3 key with associated_data=certificate.

delete.description:
X-Server-Key authenticates server and resolves its delivery profile. Bound profile required. sub takes precedence over uid; pairwise profile permits sub only. Public mode accepts an existing public UID; pairwise sub resolves in its sector. The handler does not require a client-consent record or bound-server membership for entitlement access. Absent key succeeds. Key matches ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$; value is any valid JSON, <=4096 bytes after compaction. At most 50 keys per user/profile; updates at capacity allowed. 

Business failures use HTTP 200 with nonzero code and no data: 1 for validation/database errors, 400 for handlers using BadRequest, 401 for expired sessions, 403 for denied authority/data scope. Messages are localized. Default request-body cap is 1 MiB; known oversized Content-Length returns HTTP 413, while streaming overflow may be reported by the JSON/multipart binder.

get.description: Exactly one WECHATPAY2-SHA256-RSA2048 header with five quoted attributes: mchid, serial_no, nonce_str, timestamp, signature. Signature is base64 RSA-SHA256 (PKCS#1 v1.5) over METHOD + newline + exact RequestURI + newline + timestamp + newline + nonce + newline + exact body + newline. Self-hosted relay compatibility, not official WeChat. Approved app, configured RSA verification key/serial/APIv3 key and IP allowlist required. Authorization<=4000 bytes; timestamp +/-300 seconds; nonce 8..64 bytes, replay-protected for 11 minutes; RequestURI<=4096 bytes; body<=16000 bytes; duplicate query fields rejected. Authenticated responses include Wechatpay-* signatures using relay certificate; authenticate failure is unsigned HTTP 401 SIGN_ERROR. Signing failure may produce empty HTTP 503. Use fresh nonce for retries. Certificate is self-signed relay trust anchor, encrypted using APIv3 key with associated_data=certificate.

Administrators edit the fields through the `profile` object of the user editor.
tags.name: modules/profile

tags.description: Review-mode registry (`review`): each reviewable kind registered with it (`realname`, `server_application` (game-server onboarding), `developer_access` and `oauth_client` (self-registered OAuth apps), each while its module is loaded) is reviewed in one mode chosen on the admin page 审核方式 (`review:manage`): `manual` (a human reviews every submission; always available and the default), `auto` (approve on submit), `webhook` (a signed POST to an admin-configured URL, answered synchronously with `approve` / `reject` / `manual` / `pending` or later through `POST /api/review/callback`; errors and timeouts fall back to manual) or `provider` (real-name only: the KYC providers). A mode switch acts only on submissions filed after it: the backlog is never approved or sent automatically. Decisions go through each kind's existing approve / reject functions and apply only while the submission is still pending.
tags.name: modules/review

tags.description: User audit (`user-audit`): the per-account dossier page for administrators (`useraudit:view`) inside their user data scope; this module serves the grouped sign-in address history, the other sections read the existing audit endpoints under their own permissions.

tags.description: First-start install wizard (`internal/install`). While the instance is not installed the server serves only this engine: `/healthz`, a minimal `/api/config` (`installRequired`, `version`), `/api/install/*` and the SPA shell; every other backend path answers 503 with `data.installRequired`. The POST routes need the one-time setup token (printed to the log at startup and kept in the data directory's `setup-token` file) as `token` in the JSON body; 20 wrong tokens per client IP in 10 minutes answer 429. After `finish` the same listener serves the normal app without a restart, and these routes answer 404.
